summary: What happens when two keys want the same slot.

steps.say: A hash map is an array. The whole trick is turning a key into an index.
hash("cat") lands on 3. Store it there. Lookup is now one jump, not a scan.
hash("dog") lands on 7. Also fine. This is the case everyone pictures.
hash("bat") also lands on 3. The slot is taken.
Chaining: the slot holds a list, not a value. Both keys live at 3 and lookup walks the chain.

The thing that actually matters is not the collision, it is the ratio. Once entries exceed about 75% of slots, chains get long and O(1) quietly becomes O(n) — so the map resizes and every key is rehashed to a new index.
steps.aside: Collisions are normal. Long chains are the bug.
